summary: This case study details the window spreading algorithm used in SuperDimmer's v0.8 release, replacing uniform grids and perimeter walks with concentric rectangular orbits, global greedy Euclidean distance assignment, and bounded 2-opt local search. It provides clear technical architecture explanations, code snippets, and integration details regarding macOS Accessibility APIs and the private _AXUIElementGetWindow symbol.
strengths: Clearly documents the algorithmic evolution from v0.1 through v0.8 for window placement management.
Provides concrete Swift implementation code for orbit slot generation and 2-opt local search matching.
Addresses practical macOS system constraints, such as utilizing _AXUIElementGetWindow for mapping CGWindowID to AXUIElement.
Excludes recording and call applications correctly by bundle ID and owner name to avoid interference.
weaknesses: Lacks empirical benchmark tables for execution time across varying window counts N.
Multi-display spread is explicitly omitted from implementation scope.
Relies on a private macOS API symbol (_AXUIElementGetWindow) which introduces long-term compatibility risks.
suggestions: Include benchmark measurements for N up to 40 to quantify the time taken by greedy assignment and 2-opt passes.
Expand documentation on multi-display coordinate transformations if multi-screen support is planned.

claims.text: SuperDimmer's Spread Windows Evenly action is a one-shot deterministic layout of the windows on the primary macOS display.
claims.source: SuperDimmer GitHub repository documentation and source files

claims.text: SuperDimmer uses the private function _AXUIElementGetWindow for joining CGWindowID and AXUIElement objects.
claims.source: SuperDimmer source code file AutoMinimizeManager.swift / EquidistantSpreadService.swift

claims.text: Recording and call apps are excluded by bundle ID (us.zoom.xos, com.google.meet, com.microsoft.teams2) or owner name.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Moving macOS windows across Spaces with SIP on using CGEvent grab and System Events Control-Arrow
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Focuses specifically on deterministic spatial layout algorithms (concentric rectangular orbits and 2-opt assignment) rather than cross-Space window movement via System Events.
